title: Guardrails for External Partners, Travel, and Expense Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose

This playbook provides consolidated guardrails, approval matrices, and standard templates for engagements with external partners, travel expense handling, procurement thresholds, and access & change controls that touch third-party systems or customer data. It unifies disciplines commonly split between Security, Finance, and People Ops to reduce ambiguity during cross-functional approvals.

Scope

Applies to:
- All employees and contractors who manage or approve vendor contracts, procurements, travel bookings, or grant external access to Redwood systems or data.
- All vendors, consultants, contractors, and event-related third parties.
- All regions and deployment types (hosted, dedicated, private).

Key contacts and ownership

- Document owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team: finance-legal)
- Primary approvers: Procurement Lead (procurement@redwood.com), Legal Counsel for Vendor Contracts (legal@redwood.com), Security Owner for Access (security-ops@redwood.com)
- Operational contact for travel & T&E: People Ops Travel Desk (travel@redwood.com)

High-level principles

1) Least privilege: External access is granted for the minimum scope and period. All accesses expire automatically unless extended via a documented review.
2) Risk-based approvals: Higher dollar, higher data-sensitivity, or high-impact change requests require progressively stronger approvals.
3) Single source of truth: All approvals and contracts are recorded in the procurement system and linked to the contract artifact in the vendor registry.
4) Time-bound exceptions: Any exception to standard approvals must include a mitigation plan and an expiry date.

Quick decision matrix (summary)

- Access requests to production systems: Security approval required; SLA: standard 2 business days; emergency paths 4 hours with on-call SRE sign-off.
- Purchases < $5,000: Manager approval.
- Purchases $5,000–$50,000: Manager + Procurement review.
- Purchases > $50,000: Procurement + Finance + Legal review; procurement committee/kmc approval for strategic vendors.
- Travel international with client/customer meetings: People Ops + Manager sign-off; legal review if contract signing or demo with NDAs involved.

Access & permissions workflow (external/partner access)

1) Initiation: Requester files access request in the Access Portal (link to internal Access Portal). Include: business justification, requested resources, data access level, start/end date, and vendor contact.
2) Security triage: Security reviews sensitivity (PII/C2/C3 classification), suggests scopes (read-only, token-limited, masked).
3) Least-privilege mapping: Owner maps requested scopes to least-privileged roles; ephemeral credentials (short-lived API keys or temporary IAM roles) preferred.
4) Approval routing: Manager -> Security -> Vendor Compliance -> Provisioning.
5) Provisioning: Infra performs provisioning and registers the credential in the secrets manager (KMS/HSM integrated).
6) Review cadence: Every 90 days owner validates active external accounts; any inactive for 30 days will be suspended.

Change management for vendor-facing systems

- Any change that affects availability, data contract, or integration points with external partners requires a Vendor-Impact Change (VIC) request.
- VIC template (short):
  - Change owner
  - Systems affected (list)
  - Expected outage or performance impact (Y/N)
  - Backout plan (bullet points)
  - Communication plan (who, when, channel)
  - Rollout window and verification steps
- VIC approvals: Engineering/Product -> Security -> Vendor Relationship Owner -> SRE for scheduled maintenance.
- Emergency changes: Post-facto VIC submission allowed but must be documented within 24 hours.

Data handling & classification for partner data

All partner data that is received, stored, or processed must be labelled according to the Redwood Data Classification standard: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Restricted data: requires encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (CMK), DLP scanning on ingress, and a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
- Processing rules: No partner data classified Restricted may be processed in developer laptops or unapproved sandbox environments.

Procurement and expenses (partner programs & travel)

Approval thresholds and routing (table described below):
- Under $5k: Manager approval (expense report or purchase order).
- $5k–$50k: Procurement review + Manager (attach vendor questionnaire).
- $50k–$250k: Finance + Procurement + Legal review; require 2 bids unless sole-source justification provided.
- Over $250k: Executive procurement committee review and director-level sign-off.

Typical timeline expectations:
- Standard vendor onboarding and PO issuance: 7–14 business days.
- Contract execution with Legal review: 10–21 business days depending on negotiation.

Travel & T&E specifics

- Booking: Employees must use the company travel portal unless approved by People Ops for specific itineraries.
- Per-diem (examples):
  - Domestic travel (US): $75/day lodging cap unless pre-approved higher rate for conferences; meals $60/day.
  - APAC business travel: lodging cap varies by city (Tokyo/Seoul/Singapore $180/day), meals $65/day.
  - International client travel: submit itinerary and risk assessment 7 business days before departure.
- Expense reporting: Submit within 10 business days of trip completion. Receipts required for all items >= $25; card swipe + merchant receipt acceptable.
- Travel insurance: Required for international travel longer than 5 business days or when employee will access private client facilities.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum items)

1) Vendor profile: legal name, tax ID, jurisdiction, point-of-contact.
2) Security questionnaire: completed and reviewed (minimum secure score threshold = 75%).
3) Contract & DPA: Signed and uploaded to contract registry.
4) Insurance evidence: general liability and cyber insurance where applicable.
5) Financial vetting: for spend > $50k, credit check or references.
6) SLAs and escalation path: Define contact, hours, and support expectations.

Exception and emergency approvals

- Short-lived exceptions (<= 30 days) may be approved by Procurement + Security with a documented mitigation and stakeholder notification.
- Long-lived exceptions (> 30 days) require Legal + Director-level approval and quarterly evidence that mitigations are in place.

Templates and examples (included inline for copy-paste)

1) Vendor access request (YAML):

requester: jane.doe@redwood.com
vendor: Acme Analytics Inc.
resources: ["prd-api-cluster-42", "s3:customer-dumps/partner-x"]
justification: Automated ingestion for customer reporting; data reduced to pseudonymized CSV
data_classification: Confidential
start_date: 2026-03-01
end_date: 2026-06-01
approvers: ["manager@redwood.com", "security-ops@redwood.com"]

2) Procurement checklist (bullet form):
- Business need summary
- Estimated spend and billing cadence
- Vendor questionnaire score and red flags
- Contracts and termination clauses
- Payment terms and tax treatment

Escalation paths and SLAs

- Access provisioning SLA: 2 business days standard; emergency 4 hours with on-call owner.
- Procurement turnaround: Standard PO issuance 7–14 business days; expedited path (executive sponsor required) 48–72 hours.
- Security incidents involving vendor data: Incident line (incident@redwood.com) and Security on-call within 60 minutes.

Operational playbook maintenance

- This document will be reviewed quarterly by Finance & Legal and Security to update thresholds, per-diem rates, and approval flows.
- Owners must maintain the accompanying templates folder (link to templates) and update the Access Portal mapping.
